desc:
Look at all distinct non-empty strings that can be obtained as a subsequence of s, and sort them in dictionary order (a string comes before every longer string that starts with it). Return the k-th string in this order (counting from 1), or "-" if there are fewer than k such strings.

For example, for s = "aba" the distinct subsequences in order are a, aa, ab, aba, b, ba, so k = 4 gives "aba" and k = 7 gives "-".
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Generating all subsequences is hopeless. Build the answer letter by letter instead, like looking up a word in a dictionary, and count how many strings start with each candidate letter.

To count distinct subsequences without double counting, always match a letter at its first occurrence after the current position. Let f[i] be the number of distinct subsequences of s[i:] including the empty one; then f[i] = 1 + sum over letters c of f[next(i, c) + 1].

Walk through letters a..z at the current position: the strings starting with letter c number f[next+1]. If k is within that count, take c (the string c alone is the first of them), otherwise subtract the count and try the next letter. Cap the counts at about 2·109 to keep numbers small.
editorial: Precompute nxt[i][c], the first index at or after i where letter c occurs (or -1). Any distinct subsequence corresponds to exactly one greedy embedding that always uses the earliest possible position, so counting along these embeddings counts each distinct string once. With f[i] as the number of distinct subsequences of the suffix s[i:] including the empty one, we get f[n] = 1 and f[i] = 1 + ∑c f[nxt[i][c] + 1]. These numbers explode, so cap them at a bound larger than the maximum k; capping is safe because we only compare them with k.

Now descend like in a trie. At position pos, try letters in alphabetical order. The strings that begin with c (using its first occurrence j) number f[j+1]. If k ≤ f[j+1], the answer starts with c: if k = 1 the string c itself is the answer, otherwise subtract 1 for it and continue from pos = j + 1. If not, subtract f[j+1] and try the next letter; if no letter is left at the top level, the answer is "-". Table and counts cost O(26 n); the descent costs O(26 n) as well. Memory O(26 n).
